clean.tx: bo ikʊgona munkiina mula∼mula ɪnjala jan̩dʊmaga fiijo, alɪnkʊtendeela pamwanya ʊkʊtɪ asooke abʊʊke nkʊlya. alɪnkwaga ɪngiisi jɪlipo ngatɪ mundʊ ɪɪmilepo, ngɪmba iisyanjʊ lɪn̩gwɪliilepo
clean.tl: While he [Hare] was staying there in the pit, he was plagued by hunger. He had a look upwards to leave and go to eat. He found there was darkness, as if a person was standing there, in fact a leaf had fallen (there) on him.' [Saliki and Hare]

clean.tx: piisɪɪlya aalyandile ʊkʊbopa kɪsita kʊkeetako kʊʊnyuma
clean.tl: On the other side, he started to run without looking back.

clean.tx: nkamu gwangʊ Pakyɪndɪ, ɪɪng’ombe sikoonanga fiijo amajabʊ gaako akabalɪlo akaa pamuusi, ngʊkʊsʊʊma ʊkʊtɪ ʊbʊʊke ʊkasigɪleko paapo amajabʊ goonangiike fiijo
clean.tl: My friend Pakyindi, the cows are destroying your cassava during the day, I beg you go and have a look there, because the cassava is very spoiled.

clean.tx: ikwega ɪnjɪnga, akabagɪla pakʊpota, paapo afuleele ɪkɪlʊndɪ. ikʊsookapo.
clean.tl: He takes the bike, he cannot ride it, because he has injured his leg. He sets off.

clean.tx: ɪfinyamaana ɪfi fyamanyeene fiijo nɪmbombo syabo syosa fyatʊʊlanaga
clean.tl: These animals were close friends and helped each other with everything.

clean.tx: kalʊlʊ nʊlʊbʊbi balɪnkʊjobana kʊkʊmwanya kʊmpiki
clean.tl: Hare and Spider talked high in the tree.

clean.tx: paapo baaliitɪkeene na kalʊlʊ ʊkʊbopa amaeli mahaano
clean.tl: Because they (Tugutu and Hare) had agreed to run five miles.

clean.tx: jʊla ikwitɪkana nanuuswe
clean.tl: That one agrees with us.

clean.tx: twandile ʊkʊmoga
clean.tl: We have (just) started dancing.

clean.tx: tʊmalile ʊkʊmoga
clean.tl: We have (just) finished dancing.

clean.tx: tʊlekile ʊkʊmoga
clean.tl: We have (just) stopped dancing.

clean.tx: ikʊgaala
clean.tl: S/he is getting drunk.

clean.tx: alɪ pakʊfika
clean.tl: S/he is arriving.

clean.tx: akaalɪ ikʊfika
clean.tl: S/he still arrives (regularly).

clean.tx: naatima ɪɪng'ombe pakaaja
clean.tl: (intended: When I am grown up, I will build a big house. Then I will herd cows at home.')

clean.tx: bo mmalile pakʊkina naabʊʊka kʊnnuguna gwangʊ kʊkʊlya nagwe ɪfindʊ fya pamuusi
clean.tl: (intended: Tomorrow I will play football. When I am done playing, I will go to my younger brother to have lunch with him.')

clean.tx: paapo mwe baana ʊmwe mulɪ bapɪɪna, baliko abanyambala bamo aba bisakʊbasyobaga nʊkʊpeefya
clean.tl: Because your are orphans, there are some men who might try to persuade you.

clean.tx: babapege ɪfindʊ nʊtʊndʊ ʊtʊngɪ ʊkʊtɪ mulogwege nabo
clean.tl: They will give you food and presents so that you have sex with them.

clean.tx: Saliki alɪnkʊtɪ ʊm̩buutile kalʊlʊ ʊjʊ ndile ʊbuutege?” ʊnkasi gwa Saliki alɪnkʊtɪ keeta ʊtile baatɪ nheesya gwɪtu!? num̩buutiile ɪngʊkʊ. alimo nnyumba, alɪ pakʊlyamo”
clean.tl: Saliki said “Have you slaughtered Hare, whom I told you to slaugher?” Saliki's wife said “Look, you said he is our guest!? I slaughtered a chicken for him. He's in the house, he's eating.”

clean.tx: baatɪ ngʊsʊʊma ɪɪkook”
clean.tl: [Quoting:] I'd like a Coke.”' [overheard]

clean.tx: fiki?” afwile ɗaaɗa gwake” nkoolele!” alɪnkʊsooka kajamba, ikʊlɪla hɪhɪhɪhɪɪ, hɪhɪhɪhɪɪ, afwile, afwile”
clean.tl: [Monkey:] Why?” [Tortoise's child:] His sister died” [Monkey:] Call him!” Tortoise came out, he is crying ”hihihihiii, hihihihii, she died, she died.

clean.tx: po mwangambɪlɪ he? baatɪ afwile ɗaada, ee? po ndaga”
clean.tl: Monkey: So your sister died, yes? My sympathy.”

flagged.tl: S/he is dressing (putting on a/the coat).

flagged.tx: po lyapɪmbaga iipango po∼poosa pala likʊbʊʊka. po lyandaga ʊkʊkʊba iipango lɪla. po abandʊ bamogege
flagged.tl: It (the monster) carried the guitar wherever it went. It would begin to play that guitar. People would then dance.
